newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CRUDE PRICES FLOUNDER ON INCREASED SUPPLIES.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CRUDE PRICES FLOUNDER ON INCREASED SUPPLIES.

text.p: Prices for U.S. domestic crude grades floundered Thursday on sentiment the supply of sweet and sour barrels from foreign sources is more than abundant, driving price differentials lower.

Outright benchmark prices for September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing slid around 35 cents to talk late Thursday at $20.05-15 a barrel. September/October spreads moved out to almost 20 cents in favor of October, loosening the Postings Plus price to around $1.85-90.
Traders said West Texas Sour/Midland remained around $1.50 under WTI late in the session, with pressure seen from expectations for renewed Iraqi oil exports in the offing.

Sweet crudes lost ground to around 12-14 cents over September WTI for Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James. North Sea Brent has cheapened, pressuring LLS, traders said. Leading the charge lower were reports of a Dated Brent deal for August 20-24 laoding at September Brent minus 20 cents, bolstering chances for bringing over trans-Atlantic shipments.
Other deals were seen for Midland/WTI at 30 and 31 cents under WTI, traders said.
Iraq was seen gaining approval for submitting oil contracts from late Friday morning, setting the stage for liftings in the next few days.
